chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Any man who buys a slave girl, has intercourse with her, and then finds a defect in her which he did not return [for], the seller shall return to him the value of the defect.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a buyer finds a defect in a slave girl after consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific ruling of *khiyar al-'ayb* (option of defect) in the context of manumission or sale of a slave girl, distinguishing it from general sales. It establishes that if the buyer retains the slave after discovering a hidden defect post-consummation, the seller is obligated to pay the difference in value (*qimat al-'ayb*) rather than accepting a return of the slave. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for defining the financial liability of the seller when the buyer chooses to keep the item despite the defect.
